authority_note: Dated September 12 re-review supersedes prior current judgments; historical raw data and studies remain immutable.
portfolio_context: Actual holding, tax basis and portfolio risk budget were not supplied in this run. No position size is invented and buy authorization remains false.
structural_thesis: Quanta is a craft-skilled, self-perform infrastructure platform positioned at the intersection of utility grid modernization, generation, large-load/data-center construction and related mechanical/electrical infrastructure. Q2 2026 revenue growth, record RPO and backlog, and higher Electric margins support a durable structural opportunity. The thesis depends on converting record demand into per-share owner cash without acquisition-led dilution, project-cost leakage or falling returns on invested capital.
current_finding: Harness-rule TTM diagnostics are approximately $32.906B revenue, $1.327B net income attributable to common stock, $3.178B operating cash flow, $0.787B capital expenditures and $2.391B mechanical OCF-minus-capex. TTM non-cash stock compensation is approximately $0.226B and the conservative OCF-minus-capex-minus-SBC diagnostic is approximately $2.165B. These are diagnostics, not normalized owner FCF, because working-capital timing, acquisition integration, project claims/change orders and future strategic capex remain material.
economic_finding: Q2 revenue was $9.56B and net income attributable to common stock was $451.4M. H1 revenue was $17.432B, up 34% YoY, with acquired businesses contributing roughly $1.73B of the year-over-year increase. June RPO was $33.55B, up 41.2% from year-end, while total non-GAAP backlog was $53.44B. RPO is the stronger contractual demand signal; backlog additionally includes estimated orders under MSAs, estimated renewals and certain non-fixed-price contracts and therefore is not treated as firm contracted revenue.
capital_and_survival: June cash was approximately $0.506B versus about $6.096B of long-term debt obligations including current maturities, plus $0.448B of commercial paper and $0.029B of revolving loans. Quanta retained approximately $2.77B of combined cash and available senior-credit commitments. H1 acquisition cash spending was $0.930B, and Phalcon/Percheron/PSD/Enerfab announced in Q2-July carried approximately $1.24B aggregate upfront consideration plus up to $0.242B contingent consideration. Operating survival is not externally dependent, but acquisition and capacity-cohort returns are central to shareholder economics.
permanent_loss_case: Utility and large-load projects are delayed after labor, fleet, manufacturing and acquisition commitments expand; backlog proves less durable than headline figures because MSA estimates do not convert as modeled; fixed-price project costs and claims compress margins; acquisition integration and goodwill fail to earn the 9% hurdle; financing costs remain elevated; and a valuation above conservative Base economics compresses while Quanta remains solvent.
falsifiers: RPO growth and conversion fall materially for multiple quarters while backlog remains supported mainly by MSA estimates rather than firm orders.
Electric segment margins fall materially while labor, subcontractor or material costs rise and project execution deteriorates.
OCF-minus-capex-minus-SBC per share fails to compound despite continued double-digit revenue growth.
Recent acquisitions fail to earn after-tax incremental returns above 9% after integration and working-capital normalization.
Unapproved change orders, claims or contract assets rise faster than revenue and cash collection weakens.
Large-load/data-center customers delay grid interconnections or projects and utility capex no longer offsets the slowdown.
Net debt or commercial-paper reliance rises persistently despite strong reported earnings.
A material accounting/control failure emerges, particularly in acquired entities and percentage-of-completion estimates.
The stock remains above conservative Base value while RPO, margins and owner cash weaken together.
increase_evidence: At least two reporting periods in which RPO conversion, Electric margins and OCF-minus-capex-minus-SBC per share improve together.
Recent acquisitions and strategic manufacturing/craft-capacity investments demonstrate post-ramp after-tax incremental returns above the 9% hurdle.
Contract assets, unapproved change orders and DSO remain controlled as revenue scales.
Large-load/data-center demand broadens across multiple customers and regions without materially weakening contract terms or margins.
Share count remains disciplined after acquisition equity consideration and compensation, with repurchases funded from excess owner cash rather than debt.
Expectation gap becomes clearly favorable through a materially lower price or materially higher normalized owner cash; price decline alone is insufficient.
sell_evidence: Two or more quarters of material RPO deterioration accompanied by project delays, cancellations or weaker cash conversion.
Project estimate revisions, claims or fixed-price losses cause persistent margin compression.
Acquisition returns remain below the hurdle after integration while acquisition cadence continues.
Owner cash per share deteriorates structurally despite backlog and adjusted-EPS growth.
Net leverage rises and external refinancing increasingly funds ordinary reinvestment rather than discretionary acquisitions.
Major data-center or utility customers reduce capital programs and replacement demand fails to offset the decline.
A material accounting or control issue undermines confidence in percentage-of-completion revenue recognition.
Valuation remains near bull economics while business-quality evidence weakens.

evidence: Q2 revenue reached $9.56B and June RPO reached $33.55B, with management citing converging utility, generation and large-load markets.
Electric remains more than 80% of H1 revenue and benefits from grid modernization, generation interconnections, data centers and manufacturing load growth.
counter_evidence: Infrastructure demand remains project-cycle, permitting, financing and regulatory dependent; 2026 growth also contains meaningful acquisition contribution.

evidence: Quanta's self-perform craft workforce, engineering, procurement, construction and program-management capabilities are valuable where schedule certainty and skilled labor are scarce.
RPO grew 41.2% from year-end and approximately 70% is expected to be recognized within twelve months.
counter_evidence: Customers can rebid projects, alter schedules and negotiate change orders; services businesses have less contractual lock-in than software or proprietary component franchises.
missing_data: Independent customer retention and project-level share-of-wallet data.

evidence: Quanta combines scale, safety record, skilled labor, fleet, utility relationships and increasingly integrated electrical/mechanical/fabrication capabilities.
Recent acquisitions expand data-center and mission-critical electrical/mechanical self-perform capabilities without dependence on one end market.
counter_evidence: The industry remains competitive and labor, fleet and execution capacity can be replicated over time by well-capitalized peers; scarcity conditions are not a permanent moat by themselves.
missing_data: Independent market-share and price-retention evidence after industry capacity normalizes.

evidence: Harness-rule TTM OCF-minus-capex is about $2.39B and conservative OCF-minus-capex-minus-SBC about $2.17B.
H1 DSO improved to 57 days from 62 days a year earlier and below the five-year historical average of 71 days.
counter_evidence: H1 OCF benefited from working-capital movements and acquisition/capacity spending continues; post-acquisition returns are not yet observable.
Revenue recognition includes estimates of contract costs, change orders and claims, requiring discipline before treating accounting growth as owner-cash growth.
missing_data: Cohort-level after-tax returns for Dynamic Systems, 2026 acquisitions and manufacturing/capacity investments.

evidence: Management has built a broader self-perform infrastructure platform through acquisitions that align with electrical/mechanical and large-load capabilities.
The company maintains liquidity and has historically integrated multiple specialized contractors.
counter_evidence: Acquisition cadence is high: 2025 acquisition cash spending was about $3.05B, H1 2026 another $0.93B, with additional Q2-July transactions. Goodwill and intangibles are material.
missing_data: Realized acquisition ROIC and synergy/cross-sell evidence by cohort.

evidence: June cash plus available senior-credit commitments totaled about $2.77B and TTM OCF was about $3.18B.
No single customer represented 10% or more of H1 2026 revenue or receivables.
counter_evidence: Long-term debt obligations were about $6.10B and Quanta uses commercial paper; project execution and working-capital demands can create cash volatility.

evidence: At the $618.73 September 10 close, the conservative Base value of about $479.64 is roughly 22.5% below price.
Under Base margin and 18x terminal assumptions, price requires approximately 11.86% annual revenue growth in years 2-10 after a $39.5B year-1 revenue base.

evidence: PwC concluded the 2025 financial statements were fairly presented and ICFR was effective; no material integrity failure was identified in reviewed evidence.
items.resolution_needed: Reassess acquired-entity controls and contract-estimate disclosures as acquisitions age into the ICFR scope.

evidence: Quanta generates substantial operating cash flow and retains revolving capacity; debt and commercial paper support discretionary acquisitions and working capital rather than operating survival.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor leverage, commercial-paper use and acquisition funding discipline.

evidence: Share count increased modestly with acquisitions and compensation but reviewed evidence does not establish persistent excessive dilution; economic SBC remains monitored.
items.resolution_needed: Track per-share owner cash and acquisition-stock consideration over multiple periods.

evidence: Growth is supported by RPO, cash flow, DSO improvement and broad Electric demand; no customer-financing mechanism was identified.
items.resolution_needed: Track DSO, contract assets, claims and RPO conversion.

evidence: No collapse is proven, but high acquisition cadence, strategic capex and material goodwill/intangibles create new capital cohorts whose post-ramp returns are not yet observable.
items.resolution_needed: Measure acquisition and capacity-cohort after-tax incremental returns against the 9% hurdle after integration and working-capital normalization.

evidence: RPO, backlog, scale and expanding self-perform capabilities do not indicate persistent moat contraction.
items.resolution_needed: Track competitive pricing, skilled-labor retention, safety, project execution and market share.

evidence: The reference price requires about 11.86% annual revenue growth in years 2-10 under conservative Base margins and an 18x terminal multiple. This is demanding but not demonstrably impossible given current RPO and revenue growth.
items.resolution_needed: PASS does not equal buy authorization; require a stronger expectation gap or higher normalized owner cash.

evidence: No customer represented 10% or more of H1 2026 consolidated revenue or receivables; end markets span utilities, power generation, technology/load centers, manufacturing and other infrastructure.
items.resolution_needed: Track large-load and utility-customer concentration as mix shifts.

evidence: Operating failure risk is moderate, but valuation above Base economics plus project-estimate risk and acquisition/capacity reinvestment can cause long-duration impairment without bankruptcy.
items.resolution_needed: Require sustained owner-cash-per-share compounding, disciplined acquisition ROIC and a materially better expectation gap before buy authorization.

attacks: Data-center and large-load projects are delayed by grid interconnection, financing or power-availability constraints.
Utility spending remains high but project margins normalize as competitors add labor and capacity.
MSA-derived backlog estimates overstate firm demand relative to RPO.
Fixed-price cost inflation and labor scarcity create negative project revisions.
Unapproved change orders and claims rise faster than collections.
Acquisition integration fails and goodwill/intangibles do not earn the hurdle rate.
Working-capital releases temporarily flatter OCF while contract assets rise.
Commercial-paper and debt costs absorb a larger share of cash.
Share issuance for acquisitions and SBC prevents per-share cash compounding.
A premium valuation compresses even if Quanta remains a high-quality infrastructure operator.
red_team.independence: Same analyst/model adversarial review; not independent committee approval.

completion_gate.scope: Research composition and audit lineage complete; unresolved facts and veto investigations are NOT marked resolved.

limits: Stored extracts and linked dated evidence are research assertions, not a new independent audit of every original filing.
Owner margins and Base values remain estimates; undisclosed reinvestment and rights items stay unresolved.

reverse_expectations.growth_basis: Year-1 revenue anchor fixed; uniform growth years 2-10 (milestone paths retain fixed capital costs).
reverse_expectations.warning: Conditional on Base margins, capital claims and terminal assumptions; not an observable unique market forecast.

review_method: Re-review all eight categories and nine vetoes using dated harness raw/evidence, reconcile latest/checkpoint differences, recompute cash scenarios and reverse expectations, refresh dated prices, retain unaffected judgments and document every score change. No macro-score mixing.
